# Code OS

Code OS is an open-source command center for local and remote development machines. Project Git inspection is read-only; process controls and the private skills repository are explicit, authenticated mutations.

Documentation: https://code-os.mlvcdn.com/docs
Skills sync: https://code-os.mlvcdn.com/skills-sync
VPS skills setup: https://code-os.mlvcdn.com/skills-sync/vps
Computer skills setup: https://code-os.mlvcdn.com/skills-sync/local
Source: https://github.com/Melvynx/code-os
Releases: https://github.com/Melvynx/code-os/releases

Core concepts:
- Discover projects, nested applications, and all Git worktrees.
- Read the complete Portly application inventory and graph CPU and resident memory for running apps.
- Detect and group Codex, Cursor, Claude, OpenCode, Aider, and Gemini process trees.
- Stop an exact Portly app or terminate an exact agent after authenticated confirmation.
- Index screenshots by feature.
- Serve an authenticated dashboard and API on loopback.
- Redirect the public root to the command center while keeping /docs public.
- Let a signed-in user trust or revoke the current exact IP without editing a file.
- Allow optional, scoped image-only bypass URLs under /media and /files for coding agents.
- Expose the dashboard through Cloudflare Tunnel.
- Synchronize ~/.agents between a VPS and computer using the documented private Git worker.
- Install a persistent Linux user service that starts at boot without an interactive login.

Security boundaries:
- Dashboard, API, private files, screenshots, and port gateways require a signed session or explicitly trusted exact IP.
- Process mutations require same-origin POST requests and exact live identifiers. Code OS refuses to terminate its own host process tree.
- The media bypass key grants only GET and HEAD image reads under /media and /files. Treat the complete ?bp= URL as a bearer secret.
- Cloudflare tokens and authentication secrets are stored in permission-restricted local files and are never returned by the settings API.
